title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Printing and Distributing the Provisions on the Wearing of Judicial Robes by People's Court Judges
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Regulations on the Wearing of Judicial Robes by People's Court Judges"

Fa Fa [2002] No. 3

All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Regulations on the Wearing of Judicial Robes by People's Court Judges" were adopted at the 1208th meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on January 24, 2002. The "Regulations on the Wearing of Judicial Robes by People's Court Judges" are hereby issued to you. Please organize study earnestly and implement them.

January 24, 2002

Regulations on the Wearing of Judicial Robes by People's Court Judges

To enhance the professional sense of responsibility of judges and further establish the image of judges' impartial adjudication, the following provisions are made concerning the wearing of judicial robes:

Article 1. Judges of the People's Courts shall be provided with judicial robes.

Article 2. Judges shall wear judicial robes on the following occasions:

(1) When trying cases in the courtroom;
(2) When attending ceremonies for the appointment of judges or the conferment of judicial ranks.

Article 3. Judges may wear judicial robes on the following occasions:

(1) When attending major foreign affairs activities;
(2) When attending major legal commemorative or celebratory events.

Article 4. Judges shall not wear judicial robes on occasions other than those specified in Articles 2 and 3 of these Regulations. No other person shall wear judicial robes on any occasion.

Article 5. Basic-level people's courts that do not yet have the necessary conditions may not wear judicial robes when trying cases in court. Specific measures shall be formulated by each High People's Court in light of local conditions.

Article 6. Judicial robes shall be properly kept and kept clean.

Article 7. In the event of any inconsistency between these Regulations and previous provisions on the wearing of judicial robes, these Regulations shall prevail.
